props.gloss_en: the stam's inference from the mishna: [offspring born] before [the mother's] redemption are indeed consecrated
from where? as the Sages taught: 'male' to include the offspring, 'female' to include the substitute
'male' -- to include the offspring
and 'female' -- to include the substitute
I have only the offspring of unblemished animals; from where the offspring of blemished ones? when it says 'whether male' -- to include the offspring of blemished animals
'whether female' -- to include the substitute of blemished animals
[offspring born] before redemption: one view -- they are consecrated to be offered
another view -- they are consecrated [only] to graze
Rav Huna: those [born] after redemption -- one gathers them into a chamber and they die
for what is to be done? offer them? -- they come from the force of a rejected sanctity
redeem them? -- they are not strong enough for their redemption [money] to take hold
the West in R' Chanina's name (literal wording): close to their redemption one dedicates them for that same offering
rather say: close to their MOTHER's redemption one dedicates them for that same offering
the stam: 'close to their redemption'? -- is that to say they are subject to redemption?
what is the reason? R' Levi: a decree, lest one raise from them flocks upon flocks
Ravina: may one dedicate them for any offering he wishes? Rav Sheshet: one does not dedicate them [so]
a firstborn is not dedicated for any offering one wishes, as it is written 'but the firstborn... no man shall sanctify it'
consecrated animals whose permanent blemish preceded their consecration and which were redeemed are obligated in the firstborn [law] and the gifts
before or after their redemption, one who shears or works them does not incur the forty [lashes]
before or after their redemption, they do not make a substitute
before their redemption one commits me'ila with them; after their redemption one does not
and their offspring are non-sacred
and they are redeemed [even] unblemished
and one dedicates them for any offering he wishes
the general rule: they are like non-sacred animals in all respects; you have with them only the commandment of valuation

but if their consecration preceded their blemish, or a passing blemish preceded consecration and afterwards a permanent blemish arose, and they were redeemed -- exempt from the firstborn [law] and the gifts
one who shears or works them incurs the forty [lashes]
before or after their redemption, they make a substitute
before their redemption one commits me'ila with them; after their redemption one does not
and their offspring are sacred
and they are not redeemed unblemished
and one does not dedicate them for any offering he wishes
the general rule: they are like consecrated property in all respects; you have with them only permission to eat
the reisha's 'general rule' comes to include one who slaughters them outside -- that he is exempt
the seifa's 'general rule' comes to include its milk
the stam's inference: it is the unblemished that are not redeemed -- so blemished ones are redeemed
the stam's inference: it is for any offering that one does not dedicate them -- so for the same offering one does
Rav Huna [as the stam voices him]: the same applies -- even blemished ones are not redeemed
since the reisha taught 'redeemed unblemished', the seifa taught 'not redeemed unblemished'; since the reisha taught 'any offering he wishes', so did the seifa
